goal: Samuel Campbell's bio/resume site: answer who/what/where-now + contact in under 30s for recruiters, and give developers a distinctive interaction to play with on the first screen. Content always renders from assets/resume-data.js.
timeline_rules: Every evaluated round is snapshotted to versions/vNN/ and listed in versions/manifest.js. Turning points are featured. Visitors can open any version, step between milestones, and return to the current best in one action. Losing experiments stay in the archive.
design_spec: Designer spec (primary 'The Learning Curve', alternatives 'Patch Bay' and 'Pull a Print', 24-item backlog, guardrails) summarized in docs/design-brief.md

brief.protect: v18: Learning Curve wall (desktop climb, phone curve), chips, spotlight + deep links, round-two knot + 99% send, pitches + print, pitch bar, register scrubber + compare, help/belay, night, auto-belay, offline, share card, and the regression suite (loop scripts r2–r18).
brief.weakness: Main-page code is ~86KB uncompressed vs the designer's 60KB budget. The night theme CSS, the developer layer (help/belay) and the register scrubber load for everyone even though most visitors never use them.
brief.experiment: Split for speed: move night-theme CSS into assets/night.css loaded only when night is active, and the help/belay + register scrubber code into assets/extras.js loaded on first use (? key, belay, or register scrolled into view). Keep all regression tests green.
brief.expected_payoff: First-load HTML+CSS+JS drops toward the 60KB budget, with no visible change and every interaction still passing.
brief.question: Can the budget be met through loading strategy alone, without cutting features?
also_consider: A 4th direction worth testing: a 'pair-programming' chat-style front door that answers recruiter questions from resume-data.js (no AI, just matching)
Replace the placeholder AgFirst bullet and tags once Samuel supplies real highlights; regenerate assets/og.png afterwards
Turn the regression scripts into a committed tests/ folder so they ship with the repo

history.title: Three concepts
history.lesson: Content model is solid; the front door is a chooser.

history.title: The Learning Curve
history.lesson: One strong interaction beats a menu. Drag, keyboard, rail and hold-taps all work. Weak spots: CLS 0.10 on desktop from font swap, chalk bag clips mid-row, the bag change is instant so the skill story is easy to miss.

history.title: Skills you can watch pile up
history.lesson: Motion that carries meaning works: chips make the curve's y-axis legible. Kept it cheap (WAAPI, no library) and fully skipped under reduced motion. On phones the summit CTA duplicated the main buttons, so it shrinks to just Copy address.

history.title: Spotlight a skill, share the view
history.lesson: Making the rack a filter for the wall connects the below-the-fold content to the hero. Found and fixed a race: the idle hint was yanking the token back after a spotlight. Long unbroken tokens in bullets needed overflow-wrap on phones.

history.title: Patch Bay (alternate direction)
history.lesson: A puzzle in front of the facts slows recruiters, and a matrix of 32 cables is less legible than one spotlight. The 'NO CARRIER: COBOL lives at …' microcopy is worth stealing for the spotlight. The Learning Curve stays the foundation.

history.title: Round two & the 99% send
history.lesson: Specific beats generic. The floating badge crowds the narrow phone route, so on phones the 99% moves into the card instead. Measuring CLS sources showed the real culprit was late-filled text in a centered grid, not fonts.

history.title: Scrub the register
history.lesson: Previews make the archive worth visiting. Lazy-loading the iframe only when the section is on screen kept the home page light, and embedded previews skip their own register to avoid nesting.

history.title: Pull a Print (alternate direction)
history.lesson: Typography and one-job-per-page pacing are the zine's real wins. The pull is delightful but hides essentials. Rapid page flips needed a pending-target fix. Worth merging: a calm pitch-by-pitch reading mode for the résumé section.

history.title: Phone-first: the curve on its side
history.lesson: Designing for the thumb beat shrinking the desktop. Separating horizontal-scrub from vertical-scroll intent (8px, dominant axis) was essential; tested with real touch events. On a phone the horizontal curve reads even more like a learning curve than the vertical climb.

history.title: Pitches, borrowed from the zine
history.lesson: Borrowing one idea from a losing direction strengthened the winner. Testing print with a real PDF exposed that the first check had been rendered in screen mode by mistake; under print media it went 3 → 2 pages after trimming the intro.

history.title: climb --help & belay check
history.lesson: Hidden layers add delight at near-zero cost to the main path. Native <dialog> gave focus trap + Esc for free. The belay zones made the drag snapping logic visible, which is useful for tuning too.

history.title: Pitch bar navigation
history.lesson: A persistent section index is worth its 56px on phones. The bigger win was the bug it surfaced: test fixed elements after scrolling, not just at load. Also fixed: rack chip rows were not wrapping on phones since v1.

history.title: Compare any version with the summit
history.lesson: Side-by-side previews make 'why it changed' land faster than prose. Scaling two 1280px iframes into half-width boxes stays sharp enough to read headings.

history.title: Night climb
history.lesson: Keeping the paper cards made the dark theme feel like the same site. Caught a CSS gotcha: a background shorthand with a color in a non-final layer is invalid and silently dropped; measured contrast exposed it immediately.

history.title: Auto-belay (watch it climb)
history.lesson: A guided mode complements rather than duplicates when it adds information (the captions). Same trap as v5's knot: buttons inside the route must be excluded from drag-start. On phones, caption placement needed the empty lower-right of the curve so it never covers holds.

history.title: Works offline
history.lesson: Network-first for everything is the safe default for a site that changes every round; cache-first assets would have paired fresh HTML with stale JS after deploys. The size budget is now the clearest technical debt: the night theme and accumulated features doubled the CSS.

history.title: Weight diet (regression-tested)
history.lesson: Cruft was small; features are the weight. A standing regression suite (one action script per round) made the cleanup safe, and it's now the gate for every future round. Remaining budget gap (~86381 vs 60000 bytes uncompressed, ~25KB gzipped) is recorded as known debt.

history.title: One site, many rooms
history.lesson: Consistent wayfinding is cheap and makes the modes feel like part of one site. Inside archived snapshots, links to the register must escape the snapshot folder; the bar now detects that.

history.title: Share card
history.lesson: The first impression extends to places the site doesn't control. The OG image is a snapshot of data, so it must be regenerated when the résumé changes (documented in tools/og-card.html).

biggest_wins: v1 replaced a chooser with a first-screen interaction that answers who/what/now
v3 turned skills into a filter with shareable deep links
v5 made the wall specific to Samuel (round two knot, 99% send) and cut CLS to 0
directions_tried: Learning Curve climbing wall (v1–v3, v5, v6)
Patch Bay hardware matching game (v4, rejected)
cycle_reviews.getting_repetitive: Bolting more widgets onto the route card (summit strip, compare view, send tag). The card is near capacity on phones.
cycle_reviews.next_cycle_ambition: Test the third design direction (Pull a Print zine) for real, then rework the phone hero as its own layout instead of a squeezed desktop grid, and try a navigation change (pitch-by-pitch scrolling).

v11 pitch bar plus the fix for a hidden viewport-widening bug that had been pushing fixed UI off-screen since v8
v9 proved a losing direction (the zine) can donate its best idea to the winner
directions_tried: Pull a Print editorial zine (v7, rejected)
cycle_reviews.getting_repetitive: Small add-on layers (help overlay, compare toggle, register polish). Useful, but each adds less.
cycle_reviews.next_cycle_ambition: Try a different visual style (a night/headlamp mode), a different core interaction for passive visitors (an auto-belay story mode that climbs and narrates), and harden performance/offline. End with a full verification pass.

cycle_reviews.getting_repetitive: Polish passes and add-on layers. The wall is close to feature-complete; more widgets would crowd it.
